signature.one_line: Two-shot POV skit: persistent mid-frame label, rant, jump cut to polite phone voice.
unique_devices: Single persistent 'POV: <premise>' label in white medium sans dead-centre at 49.8 % H, ~81 % W, from frame 0 to the last frame
Tonal flip at ~30 % of runtime: frustrated outburst, soft jump cut mid-sentence to the polite professional voice
Propped-phone static medium shot, no captions, grade or music: the audio contrast is the joke
signature.why_it_works: The label frames every viewer as the subject; the instant mood flip is a recognisable truth about customer-facing jobs and lands before a swipe.

hook.type: In medias res (POV label + visible meltdown)
hook.first_frame: one person at a laptop seen from a low propped-phone angle, blank stare, white 'POV:' label line across the chest at mid-frame

structure.what: typing, blank stare under the persistent POV label
soft jump cut to the same person answering a call in a bright professional voice

background_text.how: one line, 'POV:' caps + lowercase premise, Poppins 500 67 px white, very faint shadow, centred at 49.8 % H, ~81 % W; static, screen-fixed, no animation

layout.how: propped phone at desk height, subject centred; label crosses the chest below the face

transitions.how: same framing, a few frames of blend; skips from rant to phone call

other_text_spec.type: persistent POV title (no speech captions; the only text)

spec.punctuation: colon after POV; no full stop

grouping.sync: not tied to speech; on from frame 0 to the last frame

layout.note: sits across the subject's chest/shoulders, below the face

title.font_class: neo-grotesque / humanist-geometric sans, medium (two-storey a, straight-tailed y, slanted t cut)

closest_match.web_font: Poppins Medium (alt Montserrat Medium; the native short-video app face is closest to a semibold humanist-geometric sans)

title.shadow: very faint soft shadow, barely visible (estimated 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.25))
title.k_note: 'POV:' (caps, k 0.73) 2.7 % -> 71 px; a full ~24-character line with descenders measured 3.44 % H / 81.1 % W -> 67 px (descender ink over light clothing is partly lost, +/-0.2 % H)
title.verified_note: 67 px keeps both the 'POV:' calibration and a full ~24-character line (~81 % W) inside +/-0.5 % H / +/-2 % W; a larger size overflows ~84 % W

animation.exit: on to the last frame; unaffected by the soft jump cut at ~30 % of runtime

other_text_spec.text: no captions, logos, watermark or end card

style.look_intent: mid-contrast, natural-saturation, warm; ungraded indoor phone light with cool window daylight

sound.music: possible music bed (heuristic, ~103 BPM estimate) under raw dialogue; keep dynamic

sound.method: heuristic (onset-envelope beat periodicity + level in speech gaps); not a classifier

catalog_styles.name: Big-Text Hook
catalog_styles.role: one persistent label as the only text

catalog_styles.name: Jump-Cut Editing
catalog_styles.role: single jump cut that delivers the flip

catalog_styles.name: Sound-Effect-Led Reveal (SFX Punch)
catalog_styles.role: voice-tone contrast as the punchline (no added SFX)

use_when: a relatable workplace / customer-facing joke with a before/after mood flip
a single performer, one static camera, micro length
brand wants personality content for its team or industry
avoid_when: the speech carries information that needs captions
profanity is off-brand (the format leans on a raw outburst)
brand_prompt:
Use /video-pipeline with /video-captions on videos/<project>. Apply style blueprint B05 (video-reference-match/references/blueprints/B05.json) to this brand.

BRAND TOKENS (use the brand's colour for each role; keep the contrast relationship — text and accent must stay >= 4.5:1 / >= 3:1 against what sits behind them on the footage):
- {{TEXT}}      default #FFFFFF (POV label)
- {{ACCENT}}    default #FFFFFF (no accent in this style)
- {{ACCENT_2}}  default none
- {{SURFACE}}   default none
- {{CARD_BG}}   default none
- {{FONT_DISPLAY}} default Poppins 500
- {{FONT_BODY}}    default Poppins 500
- {{HANDLE}}    default @handle
- {{LOGO}}      default the brand's logo file (transparent PNG/SVG)
Label must stay >= 4.5:1 on the footage at mid-frame; if the subject wears white, add the faint shadow (0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.25)) or darken clothing, never a box.
Canvas 1080x1920, 30 fps.

CAPTIONS
1. No speech captions.

OTHER TEXT
2. One persistent label from frame 0 to the last frame: 'POV:' in caps + a short lowercase premise (placeholder 'POV: headline here'), {{FONT_DISPLAY}} at 67 px, {{TEXT}}, tracking 0, very faint soft shadow, no stroke / box, one line centred at 49.8 % H (~81 % W for ~24 characters). No animation; unaffected by cuts.
3. No {{LOGO}}, watermark or end card ({{HANDLE}} only if required, small, outside the label band).
4. Edit: one propped-phone medium shot; frustrated beat first, then a soft jump cut at ~30 % of runtime to the polite/professional beat. No music required; keep the audio dynamic so the tone flip is audible.

GRADE
Grade from the user's footage (video-style / grade.py); target look: mid-contrast, natural-saturation, warm; natural indoor phone light.

VERIFY before rendering
a) Render the label and measure: python3 video-reference-match/scripts/caption_probe.py <test-render> --out <dir> --at <t> --box 0.05,0.47,0.95,0.53 --ink "{{TEXT}}:60"
   Expected (±0.5 % H, ±2 % W) with Poppins 500 at 67 px: 'POV:' ink ~2.66 % H / ~14 % W; a ~24-character line ~81 % W.
b) python3 video-reference-match/scripts/fit_font.py --font "Poppins 500" --word "<your label>" --ink 3.44 -> ~64-67 px for a line with descenders; if at_verified_px width exceeds ~85 % W, shorten the premise rather than shrinking below ~60 px. (fit_font.py needs a target: --ink and/or --width; it returns the px that reproduces that ink for YOUR word plus the width it will read at that px. Requires Pillow.)
c) Position within ±1 % H: label centre 49.8 %.
